schedule.strategy: Linear block index is ((t*NB+hb)*DQ+dq). Adjacent dq CTAs gather the same KV rows; this creates cache reuse opportunities without a co-residency guarantee.
For block index worker_id, grp=K-1-worker_id. Reverse ordering is local to this range; each worker receives one full group.
For block index worker_id, t=K*GT+worker_id. The launch offset is added before token decoding; no prefix token is repeated.
For block index worker_id, grp=K-1-worker_id. Reverse ordering is local to this range; each worker receives one full group.
For block index worker_id, grp=NG-1-worker_id. Descend only within the remainder range; no prefix work is reassigned or repeated.
Each block index is its token index; each CTA traverses the whole selected key range independently.
For block index worker_id, grp=ceil_div(T,GT)-1-worker_id. Reverse group order does not imply simultaneous residency or any sharing between CTAs.
Linear block index is (((t*S+s)*NB+hb)*DQ+dq). Adjacent dq CTAs request the same KV rows; this ordering creates reuse opportunities without a co-residency guarantee.

For block index worker_id, t*NB+hb=T*NB-1-worker_id. Reverse order can move longer causal rows earlier; it does not guarantee concurrent residency, balanced durations, or sharing between adjacent CTAs.
For block index worker_id, grp=ceil_div(T,GT)-1-worker_id. Reverse group order does not imply simultaneous residency or any sharing between CTAs.

verb.metadata:
Work denotes this CTA's assigned (t,hb,dq).
For P_run.cfg 2/4/5/6/7/8, (Stages,QKS,Early) is respectively
(2,16,0)/(3,32,0)/(3,32,1)/(1,0,0)/(1,32,0)/(1,32,1).
The DQ IX variants retain the cfg5/cfg8 tuple. All use KSPLIT=1.
WR1=HB/16 if QKS>0, otherwise max(HB/32,1); WC1=8/WR1;
MT1=HB/WR1 and U=KC/WC1. QHeads=0 when QKS=32 and Stages>1, else HB.
QPRE is true exactly for Stages=1 in this scope.
Early=1 first issues whole-row index loads into IndexPrefetch if IndexWidth<=1152;
wider rows use per-chunk global reads. It stages request boundaries, lengths and
topk in the future RowMax/RowSum slabs, barriers, then resolves the request and
C(t). Other configs scan metadata directly. Index loads may remain in flight
when metadata is done; metadata resolution does not consume their results.
verb.prepare:
Stage Q with zero padded heads and commit one copy group.
Use Q_shared when QHeads>0, otherwise alias ring slot zero as Q_ring.
If QPRE and Early=0, enqueue chunk zero in slot zero before waiting for Q.
Initialize control state, then publish cached indices into IndexShared when present.
Each index store depends on its register load result; query issuance need not wait for it.
Wait leaving one group outstanding only in that pre-issued case, otherwise
wait all; a CTA barrier publishes Q, control and index storage and ends metadata reads.
If QPRE and Early=1, only now enqueue chunk zero, even when the width disables index caching.
Cache the first QKS 16-wide Q slices in registers, duplicated across key groups.
When Q occupies ring slot zero, a CTA barrier after all Q fragment reads frees it.
Q_cached and any uncached Q_shared slices remain readable for the whole recurrence.
Zero Acc. For j=(1 if QPRE else 0)..Stages-2, enqueue chunk j into slot j
if j<C(t), otherwise commit an empty group.
Enqueueing a chunk resolves slot IDs in batches before issuing 16-byte row copies,
records validity and commits once; invalid slots still copy row zero of their pool.
Completion of prepare means Q is ready and priming is issued, not that KV is ready.
verb.await:
For Stages=1 enqueue c unless c=0 and QPRE, then wait all groups.
For Stages>1 wait until all but the newest Stages-2 groups have completed.
A CTA barrier then makes current Gather(c) and valid(c) readable by all warps.
verb.enqueue:
Future(c) is the prospective copy group for chunk c+Stages-1.
For Stages>1 issue it into slot (c+Stages-1)%Stages when below C(t),
otherwise commit an empty group. Stages=1 does nothing here.
For Stages>1, done means the group was committed, not that the transfer landed; it can remain
in flight through score, softmax and value. The target is initially unused or was
released by the preceding iteration's retire barrier, so no current KV is overwritten.
verb.score:
Eight warps form WR1 head groups by WC1 key groups. Each computes MT1 by U scores,
reading Q_cached where present and the remaining Q from Q_shared, plus Gather(c).
Complete the synchronous QK products, scale and mask scores, then publish per-warp
row maxima into RowMax. A CTA barrier precedes row-owner threads folding the groups
and updating m and alpha; another barrier makes those updates available to all warps.
verb.softmax:
Compute online's E, retain its unrounded sums, and store BF16 Prob. Four-lane
reductions publish RowSum; a CTA barrier makes both Prob and RowSum visible.
Row-owner threads update l, followed by a CTA barrier. Scores can then be discarded.
verb.value:
Rescale Acc, then synchronous PV reads Prob and the same Gather(c) as QK.
Each warp owns all HB rows and D/(8*DQ) distinct output columns in this CTA's slice.
Acc remains in registers across chunks; all probability/KV matrix reads finish here.
verb.retire:
A CTA barrier joins all PV readers before rotating the ring. It protects the next
writes to KV, validity, Prob and control; Q_cached remains unchanged.
verb.finish:
After the last retire, every real KV copy has been waited for and consumed;
only empty committed groups can remain. The source adds no final wait-all.
Read m, l and sink2 to form finalize's inverse; each warp scales its Acc
columns and converts to BF16 Result, including padded heads. Reuse the ring
prefix as OutputStage, writing only this CTA's D/DQ columns in HB by D staging.
A CTA barrier publishes Result, then cooperatively copy the owned columns
of real heads into out. Global stores may remain pending when individual
threads finish; attention.kernel_done provides output visibility.
There are no scratch statistics or duplicate inter-CTA stores. This worker
takes no second worktile and retains no numerical state for another call.

verb.produce:
For an in-range sample, the first GT participants resolve SelectedCount,
SwaCount and RequestId into ProbeMeta; rendezvous before checking usability.
An out-of-range or unusable sample writes the final -1 from one participant,
without initializing or reading the hash state. A usable sample clears
ProbeHash, ProbeMembership and ProbeCount, then rendezvous before inserting.
All participants share a 4096-entry open-addressed table of pool-tagged keys.
A slot has one membership byte for up to eight queries. Apply probe's
Creator/First contribution rule to LocalCount: atomicCAS publishes a new
entry before its creator sets the membership bit; matching participants
use the previous bit returned by atomicOr, without waiting for the creator.
Each nonzero local count is flushed into ProbeCount once.
Each participant prefetches one next selected index into PrefetchedId before
processing the current key; invalid IDs skip the hash operation. No index row,
query or latent is staged for reuse by either attention phase.
After the counting rendezvous, form probe's scalar ratio and write only this
sample's mapped slot once from one participant. There is no device reduction
across samples. This publication does not assert that every CTA has finished;
all local reads and stores retire by probe.kernel_done. The static resources
are per CTA, and no next worktile reuses them.

verb.build:
Union denotes UnionKey, UnionMask and the two pool counts for this grp.
All eight warps resolve each token's A and Klen into TokenExtent and issue
Q copies, zeroing padded rows. Clear the 8192-word uint64 HashTable in the
ring and the membership array. Stage the G complete sparse-index rows into
IndexStage using asynchronous copies; wait for those copies and the earlier
Q copies, then rendezvous before reading indices. Only the selected slot
intervals feed the union; invalid markers contribute no entry.
Each thread prefetches its next item before its current hash operation.
Use open addressing: atomically install the pool-tagged key, allocate its
canonical entry and publish the key/position pair in one atomic word.
A same-key contender waits for that position publication. Atomic membership
updates share the canonical entry across tokens; an already-set token bit
allocates a private extra entry, as defined by gather.
SWA entries allocate upward from slot zero and compressed entries downward
from slot 2559. Logical entries [0,Ns) use their identical physical slots;
entry k in [Ns,Nu(grp)) uses slot 2560-Ng+k-Ns. This reverses the compressed
allocation order in the logical traversal; it does not move union bytes.
A CTA rendezvous publishes keys, masks and counts and ends all HashTable
and IndexStage reads. Their ring storage is now free for the first gather.
The 65536-byte table plus 4*GT*IndexWidth index bytes fits the 131072-byte
ring by the host's GT*IndexWidth<=2560 gate.
verb.prepare:
Work(v) is the nonempty group's execution setup; RG=16 for prefix. Acquire
512 TMEM columns, initialize m_initial, l_initial, sink2 and alpha from
online, and initialize completion protocols. Only m_initial is read into
the replicated register state; alpha is first initialized to one.
Q completion, a proxy fence and CTA rendezvous publish Q and control before
done. Acc is initialized by the first PV, not by reading new TMEM.
Acc's two 256-column output halves occupy disjoint lane halves of columns
0..255; each Partial uses its reserved score columns. All four score regions
remain reserved throughout this nonempty worktile; unused lanes are unread.
The source aliases allocation metadata and union keys with live transfer
barriers; this design retains the separately budgeted objects and their
lifetimes without depending on those erroneous implementation aliases.
verb.zero:
For the empty union, all eight warps overwrite every real output row
with finalize's zero result. Q copies have completed in build:Union.
This path acquires no TMEM and initializes no transfer barriers; it creates
none of the v- or c-indexed actions. Stores complete by the containing kernel's completion.

load.meaning:
Read UnionKey and UnionMask through the two-block logical-to-physical
mapping, write Mask(c), and issue the complete Gather(c) tile.
Unless mixed(c), each of 128 loaders issues one 512-byte TMA gather4 for
four rows in one 64-element latent plane using the first entry's pool map.
Each issuer arms its own transaction bytes before that request. The single
possible mixed-pool chunk uses batched keys and 16-byte asynchronous copies
with per-loader completion arrivals. Both forms transfer the padding rows
specified by gather and fill the same swizzled tile. done guarantees all
tile data has landed; issuing later actions need not wait for it.

verb.publish:
Rendezvous all loader warps after the current gather instructions
and membership stores have been issued; publish Mask(c) with one
CTA-level arrival and the required proxy ordering. This does not
wait for Gather(c) to land. It precedes issuing the next gather.

verb.online:
A softmax warp owns its consecutive RG matrix rows. Its two
lane halves hold the two 32-key halves and duplicate m,l; read
both Partial(c,a), add and scale, select the membership bit floor(r/H),
then compute online's masked E and state updates. Exchange the two key-half maxima and sums within
the warp. Publish alpha once per row and rendezvous the warp.
Scores are replaced in place by E; both score partials have
been read when done. E remains live until publish:Prob(c).
verb.rescale:
For c=0 do not read or write Acc. For c>0 wait for the preceding
PV even if every scale is one; then conditionally rescale this
warp's rows of both output halves. The group predicate is uniform
across the warp, and all TMEM reads and writes finish before done.
verb.publish:
Narrow this warp's E to its rows of Prob(c), fence the shared
writes and TMEM rescale, then arrive once on probability readiness.
done publishes only this warp's rows and releases its score reads.
Four such arrivals jointly authorize PV and score-slot reuse.

pv.meaning:
Lane zero issues both 256-column PV output halves. Each starts
from zero on chunk zero; later chunks accumulate into the
rescaled Acc. Its per-issuer completion group covers all prior
PV operations, independently of both QK issuers. done guarantees
Acc is written and all reads of Prob(c) and Gather(c) have ended.

verb.stage:
After the final PV, compute finalize's inverse from the lower
key-half state and sink2, share inv across the warp, read both
output halves and stage only this warp's real BF16 Result rows. OutputStage
aliases the retired KV ring with a D+8 BF16-element row pitch.
Padded rows participate in convergent TMEM reads but perform no BF16
conversion or staging. done ends these reads and publishes the staged
rows; staging does not wait for the loader's empty tail commit.

qk.meaning:
Lane zero issues the half a named by Partial(c,a), covering all
MR rows and KC keys. The first product overwrites its score
region. Both issuers commit separately to a two-arrival QK
completion notification; both done events use that shared
notification, covering the partial writes and Q/Gather reads.
Neither issuer shares the PV completion group.

verb.store:
Rejoin all eight warps at a CTA barrier after the real Result rows
are staged. Cooperatively copy nrows contiguous rows from OutputStage
into out, mapping row r to token t0+floor(r/H) and head r mod H.
TMEM may be deallocated by its owner after that barrier while other
warps copy, since copy-out no longer reads TMEM. Global stores can
remain pending until the containing kernel's completion. No worker takes another
worktile.

verb.metadata:
Work is the assigned batch token t. UM=KM/8=16: the eight warps each own
HB heads by UM keys for QK and HB heads by D/8 columns for PV.
Issue whole-row index loads into IndexPrefetch, including zero values for
inactive lanes. The packed gate gives IndexWidth<=640, so index caching is
always enabled here. Stage request boundaries and this token's topk in
RequestBounds, and sequence lengths in RequestLengths; B<=32 fits the slabs.
Rendezvous before resolving the request and CM(t). Index loads may remain
in flight at done; metadata does not consume their results.
verb.prepare:
Issue the query copies into Qm, zero padded heads and commit the query group.
Initialize control from mma_online and publish the prefetched indices into
IndexShared, each store consuming its loaded register. Wait for query copies
and rendezvous to publish Qm, control and indices, ending the metadata slab reads.
Only then enqueue chunk zero into the single ring slot. Enqueueing resolves
selected IDs in batches from IndexShared, records ValidM, issues 16-byte row
copies and commits once, including the row-zero substitutes from mma_gather.
Cache all 32 query fragments in registers, with one complete Q replica per
key-group warp, and zero AccM. done guarantees Q is ready and chunk zero has
been issued, while its KV copies may still be in flight.
verb.await:
For c>0 enqueue the current GatherM and ValidM as prepare describes; c=0
uses the already committed group. Wait for all copy groups and rendezvous
before any warp reads the current tile. No future chunk is issued here.
verb.score:
Compute the synchronous QK products from Q_cached and GatherM(c), then scale
and mask ScoresM. Publish per-warp maxima into RowMax and rendezvous.
Row owners combine the eight groups and update mM and AlphaM, followed by
a CTA rendezvous making both updates visible.
verb.softmax:
Evaluate mma_online's unrounded exponentials, retain their sums and write
BF16 ProbM. Four-lane reductions publish RowSum; rendezvous publishes both
arrays. Row owners fold the eight sums and update lM; a second rendezvous
completes the update. ScoresM can then be discarded.
verb.value:
Rescale all AccM rows and execute synchronous PV using ProbM and the same
GatherM(c). Each warp owns all HB rows and D/8 output columns. All matrix
reads finish by done; AccM remains in registers for the next chunk.
verb.retire:
Rendezvous all PV readers before the next gather overwrites the single
KV slot, validity, probabilities or control. Query caches remain unchanged.
verb.finish:
Every real KV copy has landed and its readers have retired. Compute
mma_finalize's inverse, scale AccM and convert ResultM, including padded
heads. Reuse the ring prefix as OutputM for the HB by D BF16 result.
Rendezvous before cooperatively copying only real heads to out. Stores can
remain pending until remainder.kernel_done. No scratch statistics are
written and this worker takes no second worktile.

verb.inspect:
Work is sample s. One lane per candidate token resolves n_a, its SWA
count and request id into GroupMeta; a CTA barrier publishes these.
All lanes determine Usable(s). An absent sample needs no metadata reads.
verb.build:
For Usable(s), zero Hash, Membership and Count, then barrier.
Hash holds a nonzero encoding of e+1 per occupied slot, zero for empty; insertion
publishes the complete key with an atomic compare-and-swap.
Collisions advance by linear probing until an empty or matching slot.
Each slot has eight membership bits, four slots per Membership word.
Enumerate occurrences in token-major compact-slot order, divided into
1024 strided lane sequences. A lane loads its first index, then in each
iteration retains the current index and issues its next index into
NextIndex before processing the current one. Consuming a prefetched
index waits for that load result; the next load may overlap hash work.
Negative IDs do no hash work. Each insertion adds one to LocalCount
and sets its query bit; an existing key adds one only if the atomic
bit-set returns that bit already set. Insertion does not inspect the
previous membership bit and does not block other updaters until it is set.
Initialize each lane's LocalCount to zero, accumulate across its sequence,
then flush a nonzero count once to Count with an atomic add.
A CTA barrier joins all flushes before Count is used for ProbeRatio.
Hash and Membership have no consumers after this build; no next index
is loaded beyond the lane's last occurrence. For an unusable sample,
build completes without accessing these resources.
verb.publish:
One lane writes the final ProbeRatio[s] directly to Gate[s], including
-1 for unusable groups. No provisional ratio is published. The write may
reach host polling before probe.kernel_done; host selection does not
wait on this action's event. The kernel completion still precedes attention.
Each CTA handles one sample and has no state carried to another call.

verb.metadata:
Work is token t. Issue the entire index row into IndexPrefetch before
staging request boundaries, lengths and topk in the future RowMax/RowSum
slabs. A CTA barrier publishes metadata; every lane then resolves the
request and C(t). B<=32 and IndexWidth<=640 here, so both caching paths
are active. Index loads may remain in flight at metadata completion.
verb.prepare:
Stage Q, including zero padded heads, into Q_shared and commit one copy
group. Initialize m, l and sink2; publish IndexPrefetch into IndexShared,
each store depending on its own load result. Wait for Q and barrier to
publish Q, indices and control, also ending the metadata slab reads.
Now enqueue chunk zero into KVStage, recording valid and committing
once. Cache all 32 query slices in Q_cached, one copy per key group,
while that gather can remain in flight. Zero Acc.
Enqueueing resolves slot IDs in batches before issuing 16-byte latent
copies; invalid and padded slots still read row zero of their pool.
Prepare completes after Q caching and gather issuance, before KV readiness.
verb.await:
Enqueue Gather(c) unless c=0, whose copy group was issued in prepare.
Wait for all copy groups and use a CTA barrier to publish Gather(c)
and valid(c). Later chunks reuse storage released by the previous retire.
verb.score:
U=16. Each of eight warps forms HB by U scores from Q_cached and its
distinct key group in Gather(c), using 32 synchronous 16-wide QK products.
Scale, mask and publish per-warp row maxima into RowMax. Barrier before
row-owner lanes fold groups and update m and alpha; barrier again to
publish the new control values to every warp.
verb.softmax:
Compute online's E, retain unrounded sums and store BF16 Prob.
Four-lane reductions publish RowSum; barrier makes Prob and RowSum visible.
Row-owner lanes update l; another CTA barrier publishes it. Discard Scores.
verb.value:
Rescale Acc, then read Prob and Gather(c) for synchronous PV.
Each warp owns every HB row and D/8 distinct output columns.
Acc stays in registers across chunks; all probability and KV reads
by this warp finish before it reaches retire.
verb.retire:
A CTA barrier joins all PV readers before KVStage, valid, Prob and control
may be overwritten. Q_cached and IndexShared remain unchanged.
verb.finish:
The last retire ends all reads of Gather; all copy groups have been waited.
Form finalize's inverse, scale Acc and convert to BF16 Result, including
padded heads. Reuse the KVStage prefix as OutputStage and barrier before
cooperatively writing all columns of real heads to out.
Stores may remain pending when individual lanes finish; attention.kernel_done
provides output visibility. There are no scratch statistics, and the CTA
takes no second worktile or numerical state into another invocation.

verb.produce:
For an in-range sample, the first GT participants resolve SelectedCount,
SwaCount and RequestId into ProbeMeta; rendezvous before checking usability.
An out-of-range or unusable sample writes the final -1 from one participant,
without initializing or reading the hash state. A usable sample clears
ProbeHash, ProbeMembership and ProbeCount, then rendezvous before inserting.
All participants share a 4096-entry open-addressed table of pool-tagged keys.
A slot has one membership byte for up to eight queries. Apply probe's
Creator/First contribution rule to LocalCount: atomicCAS publishes a new
entry before its creator sets the membership bit; matching participants
use the previous bit returned by atomicOr, without waiting for the creator.
Each nonzero local count is flushed into ProbeCount once.
Each participant prefetches one next selected index into PrefetchedId before
processing the current key; invalid IDs skip the hash operation. No index row,
query or latent is staged for reuse by the attention phase.
After the counting rendezvous, form probe's scalar ratio and write only this
sample's mapped slot once from one participant. There is no device reduction
across samples. This publication does not assert that every CTA has finished;
all local reads and stores retire by probe.kernel_done. The static resources
are per CTA, and no next worktile reuses them.

verb.build:
Union denotes UnionKey, UnionMask and the two pool counts for this grp.
All eight warps resolve each token's A and Klen into TokenExtent and issue
Q copies, zeroing padded rows. Clear the 8192-word uint64 HashTable in the
ring and the membership array. Stage the G complete sparse-index rows into
IndexStage using asynchronous copies; wait for those copies and the earlier
Q copies, then rendezvous before reading indices. Only the selected slot
intervals feed the union; invalid markers contribute no entry.
Each thread prefetches its next item before its current hash operation.
Use open addressing: atomically install the pool-tagged key, allocate its
canonical entry and publish the key/position pair in one atomic word.
A same-key contender waits for that position publication. Atomic membership
updates share the canonical entry across tokens; an already-set token bit
allocates a private extra entry, as defined by gather.
SWA entries allocate upward from slot zero and compressed entries downward
from slot 2559. Logical entries [0,Ns) use their identical physical slots;
entry k in [Ns,Nu(grp)) uses slot 2560-Ng+k-Ns. This reverses the compressed
allocation order in the logical traversal; it does not move union bytes.
A CTA rendezvous publishes keys, masks and counts and ends all HashTable
and IndexStage reads. Their ring storage is now free for the first gather.
The 65536-byte table plus 4*GT*IndexWidth index bytes fits the 131072-byte
ring by the host's GT*IndexWidth<=2560 gate.
verb.prepare:
Work(v) is the nonempty group's execution setup; RG=16. Acquire
512 TMEM columns, initialize m_initial, l_initial, sink2 and alpha from
online, and initialize completion protocols. Only m_initial is read into
the replicated register state; alpha is first initialized to one.
Q completion, a proxy fence and CTA rendezvous publish Q and control before
done. Acc is initialized by the first PV, not by reading new TMEM.
Acc's two 256-column output halves occupy disjoint lane halves of columns
0..255; each Partial uses its reserved score columns. All four score regions
remain reserved throughout this nonempty worktile; unused lanes are unread.
The source aliases allocation metadata and union keys with live transfer
barriers; this design retains the separately budgeted objects and their
lifetimes without depending on those erroneous implementation aliases.
verb.zero:
For the empty union, all eight warps overwrite every real output row
with finalize's zero result. Q copies have completed in build:Union.
This path acquires no TMEM and initializes no transfer barriers; it creates
none of the v- or c-indexed actions. Stores complete by attention.kernel_done.

verb.store:
Rejoin all eight warps at a CTA barrier after the real Result rows
are staged. Cooperatively copy nrows contiguous rows from OutputStage
into out, mapping row r to token t0+floor(r/H) and head r mod H.
TMEM may be deallocated by its owner after that barrier while other
warps copy, since copy-out no longer reads TMEM. Global stores can
remain pending until attention.kernel_done. No worker takes another
worktile.

verb.metadata:
Work denotes this CTA's assigned (t,hb,s,dq); c0,c1 use online's abbreviation.
For P.cfg 2/4/5/6/7/8, (Stages,QKS,Early) is respectively
(2,16,0)/(3,32,0)/(3,32,1)/(1,0,0)/(1,32,0)/(1,32,1).
The DQ IX variants retain the cfg5/cfg8 tuple. All use KSPLIT=1.
WR1=HB/16 if QKS>0, otherwise max(HB/32,1); WC1=8/WR1;
MT1=HB/WR1 and U=KC/WC1. QHeads=0 when QKS=32 and Stages>1, else HB.
QPRE is true exactly for Stages=1 in this scope.
Early=1 first issues whole-row index loads into IndexPrefetch if IndexWidth<=1152;
wider rows use per-chunk global reads. It stages request boundaries, lengths and
topk in the future RowMax/RowSum slabs, barriers, then resolves the request and
c0,c1. Other configs scan metadata directly. Index loads may remain in flight
when metadata is done; metadata resolution does not consume their results.
Empty c0=c1 work publishes finalize's sentinel statistics and discards any
prefetched indices without an explicit drain. No query or KV copy was issued; c is empty.
prepare and finish still have issue/done events but perform no reads or writes.
verb.prepare:
For nonempty Work, stage Q with zero padded heads and commit one copy group.
Use Q_shared when QHeads>0, otherwise alias ring slot zero as Q_ring.
If QPRE and Early=0, enqueue chunk c0 in slot zero before waiting for Q.
Initialize control state, then publish cached indices into IndexShared when present.
Each index store depends on its register load result; query issuance need not wait for it.
Wait leaving one group outstanding only in that pre-issued case, otherwise
wait all; a CTA barrier publishes Q, control and index storage and ends metadata reads.
If QPRE and Early=1, only now enqueue c0, even when the width disables index caching.
Cache the first QKS 16-wide Q slices in registers, duplicated across key groups.
When Q occupies ring slot zero, a CTA barrier after all Q fragment reads frees it.
Q_cached and any uncached Q_shared slices remain readable for the whole recurrence.
Zero Acc. For j=(1 if QPRE else 0)..Stages-2, enqueue c0+j into slot j
if it is below c1, otherwise commit an empty group.
Enqueueing a chunk resolves slot IDs in batches before issuing 16-byte row copies,
records validity and commits once; invalid slots still copy row zero of their pool.
Completion of prepare means Q is ready and priming is issued, not that KV is ready.
verb.await:
For Stages=1 enqueue c unless c=c0 and QPRE, then wait all groups.
For Stages>1 wait until all but the newest Stages-2 groups have completed.
A CTA barrier then makes current Gather(c) and valid(c) readable by all warps.
verb.enqueue:
Future(c) is the prospective copy group for chunk c+Stages-1.
For Stages>1 issue it into slot (c-c0+Stages-1)%Stages when below c1,
otherwise commit an empty group. Stages=1 does nothing here.
For Stages>1, done means the group was committed, not that the transfer landed; it can remain
in flight through score, softmax and value. The target is initially unused or was
released by the preceding iteration's retire barrier, so no current KV is overwritten.
verb.score:
Eight warps form WR1 head groups by WC1 key groups. Each computes MT1 by U scores,
reading Q_cached where present and the remaining Q from Q_shared, plus Gather(c).
Complete the synchronous QK products, scale and mask scores, then publish per-warp
row maxima into RowMax. A CTA barrier precedes row-owner threads folding the groups
and updating m and alpha; another barrier makes those updates available to all warps.
verb.softmax:
Compute online's E, retain its unrounded sums, and store BF16 Prob. Four-lane
reductions publish RowSum; a CTA barrier makes both Prob and RowSum visible.
Row-owner threads update l, followed by a CTA barrier. Scores can then be discarded.
verb.value:
Rescale Acc, then synchronous PV reads Prob and the same Gather(c) as QK.
Each warp owns all HB rows and D/(8*DQ) distinct output columns in this CTA's slice.
Acc remains in registers across chunks; all probability/KV matrix reads finish here.
verb.retire:
A CTA barrier joins all PV readers before rotating the ring. It protects the next
writes to KV, validity, Prob and control; Q_cached remains unchanged.
verb.finish:
After the last retire, every real KV copy has been waited for and consumed;
only empty committed groups can remain. The source adds no final wait-all.
Reinterpret the ring prefix as PartialStage. Stage the owned columns from Acc
in FP32, barrier, then cooperatively copy that slice to global scratch.
Identical m/l values are redundantly published by the dq CTAs; the source's
non-atomic duplicate stores have no inter-CTA ordering.
Global stores may still be pending when individual threads finish. Kernel completion
provides the successor's visibility. This worker takes no second worktile and retains
no Q, recurrence state or ring contents for another CTA or call.

prime.meaning: For a real head, each 128-thread group g issues four float4 vector loads from splits g+k*G before loading statistics, substituting register zero only for s>=S. VectorPrefetch keeps their results through the statistics reduction; done means these registers are ready. For padded heads all four pipe actions are no-ops with issue/done events and no memory reads or writes.

verb.normalize:
Load all S m/l pairs into SplitControl and barrier. Groups reduce maxima into
GroupControl, barrier, fold M, publish weights in SplitControl, barrier.
Groups reduce weighted normalizers, barrier; thread zero folds the group totals,
adds the sink and publishes inv, barrier. G groups each contain 128 threads;
thread offset v owns latent columns 4*v..4*v+3. Vector prefetch may overlap these steps.
verb.fold:
Consume VectorPrefetch with merge's value predication; then fetch remaining split
vectors four at a time and finally singly, with merge's address substitution.
Keep one float4 accumulator per thread. For G>1 publish all group vectors into
GroupPartial and barrier before group zero folds them; G=1 uses its registers directly.
verb.store:
The first 128 threads multiply by inv, convert paired values to BF16 and overwrite
the complete output row. No scratch is reset or retained as numerical state for a
later invocation. This CTA has no next worktile; final visibility is kernel_done.

verb.prepare:
Work is the assigned (t,hb); RG=16. Resolve request metadata and C(t),
cooperatively issue Q copies, initialize online's state and acquire
512 TMEM columns. m_initial and l_initial hold the initialization
values; only m_initial is read into the replicated register state.
Initialize the alpha slot to one; the first online update overwrites it.
Q copies complete and a proxy fence plus CTA rendezvous publishes
Q, control and initialized completion protocols before done.
Acc is initialized by the first PV, not by reading new TMEM.
Acc's two 256-column output halves occupy disjoint lane halves
of columns 0..255; each Partial uses its reserved score columns
with the unused lane positions left unread. All four score
regions remain reserved throughout the worktile.
The source's allocation-return word overlaps a live transfer
barrier; the resource and dependency design here does not rely
on that erroneous implementation address alias.

load.meaning:
Resolve IDs, write valid(c) and issue the complete Gather(c) tile.
Unless 0<A(t)-c*KC<KC and (A(t)-c*KC)%4!=0, each of the
128 loaders issues one 512-byte TMA gather4 for four rows in
one 64-element latent plane, using the appropriate pool map.
Each issuer arms its own transaction bytes before that request.
The straddling chunk instead uses batched indices and 16-byte
cp.async copies with per-loader completion arrivals. Both forms
transfer row-zero substitutes and fill the same swizzled tile.
done guarantees all tile data has landed through the transfer
completion protocol; issuing later actions need not wait for it.

verb.publish:
Rendezvous all loader warps after the current gather instructions
and validity stores have been issued; publish valid(c) with one
CTA-level arrival and the required proxy ordering. This does not
wait for Gather(c) to land. It precedes issuing the next gather.

verb.online:
A softmax warp owns its consecutive RG head rows. Its two
lane halves hold the two 32-key halves and duplicate m,l; read
both Partial(c,a), add, scale, mask and compute online's E and
state updates. Exchange the two key-half maxima and sums within
the warp. Publish alpha once per row and rendezvous the warp.
Scores are replaced in place by E; both score partials have
been read when done. E remains live until publish:Prob(c).
verb.rescale:
For c=0 do not read or write Acc. For c>0 wait for the preceding
PV even if every scale is one; then conditionally rescale this
warp's rows of both output halves. The group predicate is uniform
across the warp, and all TMEM reads and writes finish before done.
verb.publish:
Narrow this warp's E to its rows of Prob(c), fence the shared
writes and TMEM rescale, then arrive once on probability readiness.
done publishes only this warp's rows and releases its score reads.
Four such arrivals jointly authorize PV and score-slot reuse.

pv.meaning:
Lane zero issues both 256-column PV output halves. Each starts
from zero on chunk zero; later chunks accumulate into the
rescaled Acc. Its per-issuer completion group covers all prior
PV operations, independently of both QK issuers. done guarantees
Acc is written and all reads of Prob(c) and Gather(c) have ended.

verb.stage:
After the final PV, compute finalize's inverse from the lower
key-half state and sink2, share inv across the warp, read both
output halves and stage this warp's BF16 Result rows. OutputStage
aliases the retired KV ring with a D+8 BF16-element row pitch.
done ends these TMEM reads and publishes the staged rows; there
is no wait for the loader's empty tail commit before staging.

qk.meaning:
Lane zero issues the half a named by Partial(c,a), covering all
HB rows and KC keys. The first product overwrites its score
region. Both issuers commit separately to a two-arrival QK
completion notification; both done events use that shared
notification, covering the partial writes and Q/Gather reads.
Neither issuer shares the PV completion group.

verb.store:
Rejoin the same eight warps at a CTA barrier after all Result rows
are staged. Cooperatively copy complete contiguous output rows
from OutputStage into out. TMEM may be deallocated by its owner

attention.kernel_done. No worker takes another worktile.
